subject.title: Telegram owner commands: trusted execution mode for approval-gated actions

question: Should OpenClaw add a trusted-owner approval-bypass mode for Telegram group-origin privileged actions, and should that live as a shared exec/elevated/tool-class policy instead of a Telegram-only config key?
rationale: The source evidence proves the requested mode is absent, but deciding when a channel identity may skip approvals changes the security boundary and public config contract.

options.title: Design shared trusted-owner policy
options.body: Add a disabled-by-default shared policy with explicit sender, allowlisted group, tool-class, destructive-operation, audit, docs, and regression-test semantics across the existing approval stack.

options.title: Keep existing approval model
options.body: Decline the bypass and document that operators who want no prompts should use existing exec/elevated full policy with host approvals configured permissively.

options.title: Add Telegram-only shortcut
options.body: Implement the proposed Telegram config directly, accepting a narrower patch but higher risk of policy drift from shared approvals and elevated execution.

recommendation.title: Design shared trusted-owner policy
recommendation.body: Add a disabled-by-default shared policy with explicit sender, allowlisted group, tool-class, destructive-operation, audit, docs, and regression-test semantics across the existing approval stack.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice is primarily product/security policy and config-surface direction before the Telegram and exec approval owners can implement a safe shape.
